paragraph_content.content: Soitec

title_content.content: F1Q preview: Photonics upside priced in;

paragraph_content.content: Lower PO
Reiterate Rating: NEUTRAL | PO: 138.00 EUR | Price: 118.40 EUR

title_content.content: Photonics growing but expectations are elevated; Neutral

paragraph_content.content: Soitec reports F1Q revenue on July 28
^{th}

. We believe there is downside risk to css estimates for both Mobile, given the weak smartphone market, and Edge AI, given the high implied Photonics-SOI growth. However, we expect the overall business to recover from its FY26 earnings trough. We raise FY27-29E Edge AI but lower Mobile and Auto/Industrial ests, lowering EBITDA. Reit. Neutral with lower €138 PO (was €193) on updated SOTP valuation.

title_content.content: Street is projecting Photonics-SOI growing above industry

paragraph_content.content: We view Soitec's Photonics-related upside as priced in, with Edge and Cloud AI (of which Photonics-SOI was 42% in FY26) forecasted to grow by css at 28%/34%/43% in FY27/28/29E. This would imply Photonics revenue growth significantly higher than the 50% CAGR for FY26-29E that we model, which is based on Photonics-SOI total die area CAGR forecasts. For context, our global team projects 40%+ total optical revenue growth CAGR in data centers. Given various uncertainties including amount of NPO/CPO content growth, we lack conviction in further Photonics revenue revisions.

title_content.content: Uncertainties remain on Photonics growth assumptions

paragraph_content.content: With questions on various Photonics-SOI content assumptions hard to answer, it is difficult to project its revenue growth CAGR. Yields, transceiver speeds, changing optical engine requirements PIC sizes, NPO/CPO ramp timelines and associated content growth all present various headwinds and tailwinds to Photonics-SOI growth. We believe the implied css Photonics-SOI growth rate already prices in growth acceleration from NPO/CPO which we view to still be uncertain given the different moving parts. Finally, GlobalWafers' planned ramp in Photonics/RF-SOI has not been derisked, introducing questions on Soitec's market share position going forward.

title_content.content: Mobile recovering but at slow pace on phone price hikes

paragraph_content.content: Mobile was more than half of FY26 revenue, and given announced price hikes by smartphone-makers, we believe there is downside to css FY27E decline of 6% in Mobile revenue (we model 11% decline). RF-SOI revenue continues to be significantly impacted by elevated customer inventories, sitting at ~2mm wafers with a slowing pace of digestion due to the weak end-market. We model 19%/27% growth in Mobile in FY28/29E, reflecting gradual customer inventory digestion.

paragraph_content.content: Soitec designs and manufactures semiconductor substrates, predominantly based on silicon on insulator (SOI) technologies. Soitec has recently been diversifying into technologies such as POI, SiC and GaN. Soitec's products are key enablers and beneficiaries of many fast growing trends such as 5G communications, vehicle electrification, silicon photonics, 3D sensing and increasing demand for low power/cost processing power. Soitec is listed on Euronext Paris and is headquartered in Bernin, France.

Soitec is a leader in silicon on insulator (SOI) substrates. Recently, Soitec has moved into new areas, such as gallium nitride (GaN) & piezoelectric on insulator (POI), with silicon carbide (SiC) in development. Soitec's products are key enablers & beneficiaries of many fast-growing trends, such as optical connectivity and 5G communications. However, we still lack visibility on when customer inventory digestion will end and tariff overhang on consumer (PC/Smartphone) demand may clear.
Exhibit 1: We project 23%/29% revenue growth in FY28/29E driven by Photonics-SOI growth and RF-SOI recovery
Soitec bottom-up revenue build, FY26-29E
Exhibit 2: We lower our FY27-29E topline ests by 3-8%, resulting in 9-14% decrease in EBITDA Soitec Changes to estimates, FY27-29E

We lower our FY29E EBITDA multiple for Photonics from 45x to 25x given the recent derating in optical stocks and given uncertainty on Soitec's growth assumptions including in NPO/CPO. We apply a 10x FY29E EBITDA multiple to Soitec's other segments, contemplating peers and Soitec's strong market position in RF-SOI.

table_caption.content: Exhibit 3: Photonics-SOI has the highest multiple and majority of EV in our SOTP Soitec SOTP valuation

paragraph_content.content: Our €138 PO is based on SOTP valuation due to the diverging growth profile of Photonics relative to Soitec's other segments. We apply a 25x FY29E EBITDA multiple for Photonics and 10x for the Mobile/Auto/Edge AI ex-Photonics segments based on the multiples of the peer companies of each segment with similar growth expectations.

Upside risks are 1) revenue growth coming in faster than we currently expect driven by faster adoption of Soitec's products and a stronger cyclical upturn in demand and 2) higher operational leverage leading to upside to our EBITDA margin forecasts

Downside risks are 1) slower adoption of Soitec's technologies than we expect, 2) valuation multiple compression in the event of rising interest rates, 3) weaker-than-expected smartphone demand, 4) disruption at Soitec or customers' production facilities, 5) cyclical weakening of demand trends and 6) development of new unforeseen technologies which may take share from Soitec's technologies.
